chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch 610: Yang Na's Visit Breaks Reality
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang's peaceful reunion with Yang Na in Kangning Hospital shatters when she mentions a jade pendant he can't remember giving her. A heart-wrenching chapter where love meets a reality-bleeding horror.
og_title: The Warm Visit That Shatters Sanity
og_description: Li Huowang plans a future with his girlfriend, but a casual question about a priceless jade pendant reveals the Dao-Twisted world is closer than he thinks.
twitter_title: When a "cured" mind meets an impossible gift.
twitter_description: A tender psychiatric visit turns eerie as Yang Na asks about a jade pendant from a world Li Huowang has supposedly left behind.

lore_anchors.definition: Li Huowang's girlfriend in the modern world. Her presence represents the "normal" life he is fighting to return to, but she is increasingly entangled in the Dao-Twisted reality.
A psychiatric hospital in the modern world where Li Huowang is being treated. It stands in stark, unsettling contrast to the horrors of the Dao-Twisted World.
A metaphor for clinical depression, describing it as a constant, suffocating companion that saps all joy and cannot be willed away.
A high-value jade ornament. In this novel's context, it is a physical object originating from the Dao-Twisted World, and its appearance in the real world is a sign of reality contamination.
A very large sum of money (approx. $55k USD). The specific number grounds the supernatural horror in a tangible, impossible fact that cannot be dismissed as a hallucination.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why is Yang Na's visit so unsettling despite being sweet?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Because under the romantic warmth, a single detail—a jade pendant that Li Huowang can't remember giving her—proves that the insane world he supposedly left behind is actively bleeding into his real life with physical, valuable evidence.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is the "black dog" Li Huowang talks about?
cultural_notes_faq.a: It's a famous Western metaphor for clinical depression. Li Huowang uses it to describe Yang Na's illness with deep, personal understanding, showing his empathy and sharp analytical mind.

The chapter strongly suggests his "cure" is a fragile illusion. The appearance of the impossible jade pendant implies his perception of a separated reality is wrong, and the Dao-Twisted crisis is far from over.
